targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: V3-EXQ-828a (null-validation run-length-corrected successor of V3-EXQ-828, IGW-20260730-192): C1 (non-degeneracy) holds, C2 (peak-composite arm interior AND beating both extremes by >= 0.15 margin) FAILS -- peak arm 'residue_off' is interior (margin_vs_min=0.232, margin_vs_max=0.148, just 0.002 short of the 0.15 threshold), monotonic_direction='none'. This is INFORMATIONALLY CONSISTENT with 828's own already-scored weakens verdict (does not retract or supersede it, per this run's own docstring and design) -- a fresh, independent, higher-power (10 seeds vs prior counts, per-arm) data point at the SAME read: intact does not distinguish itself, residue_off has the best composite. Per governance's own 2026-07-29 precedent for this cluster, the ablation-contrast is treated as sufficient discriminator on its own terms; the null-validation gap is a standing design note, not a blocker to the weakens verdict -- unchanged here. HOWEVER: this run's own PURPOSE (validating the ablation-contrast against a properly-scaled autocorrelation-preserving surrogate) did NOT succeed a second time. The IGW-20260730-192 substrate fix (bump to 3600 eval-phase steps, '26% margin over the 2848-step worst-case deficit from V3-EXQ-828') was itself under-calibrated: this run's own surrogate self-diagnosis needed up to 14648 steps for the worst seed/stream -- roughly 4x more than supplied, and ~5x more than the deficit estimate the substrate fix was sized against. Recommend AMENDING the existing INV091-NULL-VALIDATION-RUN-LENGTH substrate_queue.json entry rather than a third static-number guess: either a drastically larger margin (computed from THIS run's newly observed worst case, with headroom) or -- better -- a dynamic per-run block-length computation that measures tau_max in a short pilot pass before committing to a fixed eval-phase budget, since tau_max is empirically variable across seeds/runs and a margin computed from one run's worst case does not reliably bound the next run's.

recommended_substrate_queue_entry.implementation_hint: The existing entry bumped eval-phase steps from 1500 to 3600 (26% margin over V3-EXQ-828's own 2848-step worst-case deficit). V3-EXQ-828a's own surrogate self-diagnosis shows this was still short by up to ~4x for the worst seed/stream (14648 steps needed, only 3600 supplied). Recommend either (a) a much larger static margin computed from this run's newly observed worst case (e.g. 3-5x headroom over 14648, ~45000-75000 steps) accepting higher compute cost, or (b) implement a short pilot pass per run that measures the actual tau_max for each stream/seed BEFORE committing to the eval-phase episode count, since tau_max is empirically variable across runs and no single static margin reliably bounds it.

learning_extracted: A static run-length margin computed from one run's observed worst-case tau_max does not reliably bound a different run's worst case -- tau_max is empirically variable per seed/stream, so this is the second consecutive under-calibration of the same substrate fix (827/828's original 1500-step budget, then the IGW-20260730-192 fix's 3600-step budget, both insufficient).

The surrogate correctly REFUSED to silently shorten its blocks rather than producing an invalid null check -- this is the right failure mode (loud, not silent), but it means the intended methodological upgrade (null-validated weakens) has not yet been achieved twice in a row.

The C1/C2 ablation-contrast verdict remains informative and consistent with 828 independent of the null-validation gap, per standing governance precedent for this cluster -- the missing null check does not block scoring the weakens.

Margin_vs_max failing by only 0.002 (0.148 vs 0.15 threshold) is razor-thin -- exactly the kind of result where a working null validation would matter most for distinguishing genuine structure from noise, which is why the recurring null-validation gap is worth fixing properly rather than accepting indefinitely.
